sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责为《纽约时报》旗下的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: We started this trip by going to France, where we spent time with these people who were in the
sentences.zh: 我们这次行程始于法国，在那里我们与一群人共度时光，他们处于

sentences.en: middle of this loose movement without a leader, a movement that's dying and that, for the moment, has no hope of really running things in France.
sentences.zh: 一场松散的、没有领导者的运动之中，这场运动正在消亡，而且目前看来，在法国根本没有执政的希望。

sentences.en: We then went on to Italy, where the frustration of people has been channeled into another movement, but one that has been successful at actually being elected into government.
sentences.zh: 随后我们去了意大利，那里人们的挫败感被引导到了另一场运动中，但这场运动成功地通过选举进入了政府。

sentences.en: But it's only part of a government, part of a coalition government.
sentences.zh: 但这只是政府的一部分，是联合政府的一部分。

sentences.en: They're not running things yet.
sentences.zh: 他们还未掌权。

sentences.en: In Poland, a nationalist government has actually been in power for four years.
sentences.zh: 在波兰，一个民族主义政府实际上已经执政四年了。

sentences.en: And we're here to sort of see what that does to institutions, what that does to democracy.
sentences.zh: 我们来到这里，是为了看看这对体制、对民主意味着什么。

sentences.en: We want to see what that looks like.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看那是什么样子。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Katrin Benhold.
sentences.zh: 我是卡特琳·本霍尔德。

sentences.en: Today, Poland.
sentences.zh: 今天，波兰。

sentences.en: It's Thursday,
sentences.zh: 今天是星期四，

sentences.en: June 13th.
So we go to Warsaw, Poland's capital, the biggest city in the country.
sentences.zh: 我们前往波兰首都华沙，这是该国最大的城市。

sentences.en: You guys want to go in this camp?
sentences.zh: 你们想进这个营地吗？

sentences.en: We grab a taxi, and we head over to see this newspaper.
sentences.zh: 我们打了一辆出租车，前往那家报社。

sentences.en: Is it Wiborska?
sentences.zh: 是《选举报》吗？

sentences.en: Wiborska.
sentences.zh: 《选举报》。

sentences.en: Wiborska.
sentences.zh: 《选举报》。

sentences.en: The Gazeta Wiborska.
sentences.zh: 《选举报》。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: What did you say we're here?
sentences.zh: 你说我们到哪儿了？

sentences.en: We're here.
sentences.zh: 我们到了。

sentences.en: We went inside to ask for Jaroslav Kuski, the deputy editor.
sentences.zh: 我们进去找副主编雅罗斯瓦夫·库斯基。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: I'm Claire.
sentences.zh: 我是克莱尔。

sentences.en: Most people call him Jarek.
sentences.zh: 大多数人叫他雅雷克。

sentences.en: Jarek, it's me.
sentences.zh: 雅雷克，是我。

sentences.en: We've spoken in French.
sentences.zh: 我们用法语交流过。

sentences.en: So I don't speak Polish.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会说波兰语。

sentences.en: Jarek is not super comfortable in English.
sentences.zh: 雅雷克英语不太流利。

sentences.en: So actually, this whole meeting had been arranged in French.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，整个会议都是用法语安排的。

sentences.en: We ended up speaking this strange mix of the three.
sentences.zh: 最后我们用这三种语言奇怪地混合着交流。

sentences.en: Thank you for making time.
sentences.zh: 感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Should we go and sit?
sentences.zh: 我们要去坐下吗？

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: So Jarek walks us down the hallway.
sentences.zh: 雅雷克带着我们走过走廊。

sentences.en: He's this tall, composed, pretty formal guy in his mid-50s.
sentences.zh: 他是一位身材高大、沉稳、相当正式的50多岁男士。

sentences.en: And we take the elevator up to an office.
sentences.zh: 我们乘电梯上楼去了一间办公室。

sentences.en: The newsroom at this point is pretty empty because it's late at night.
sentences.zh: 此时新闻编辑室里空荡荡的，因为已经是深夜了。

sentences.en: And we sort of all huddle on this couch in the corner of the office.
sentences.zh: 我们都挤在办公室角落的沙发上。

sentences.en: And I'm suddenly reminded of this thing that my dad used to tell me when I was growing up in Germany.
sentences.zh: 我突然想起小时候在德国时父亲常对我说的一句话。

sentences.en: My father used to say that Polish is the language of freedom.
sentences.zh: 我父亲常说，波兰语是自由的语言。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was true.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是真的。

sentences.en: During the 80s, yes, it was absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 在80年代，是的，绝对是真的。

sentences.en: And that launched him into the story of Poland's history, his paper's history, and his own history, which we realized are all linked.
sentences.zh: 这让他开始讲述波兰的历史、他报社的历史以及他自己的历史，我们意识到这些都是相互关联的。

sentences.en: We were the witness of many, many events.
sentences.zh: 我们见证了许多许多事件。

sentences.en: Tonight, the politics and the practical problems of feeding Poland.
sentences.zh: 今晚，政治和波兰粮食供应的实际问题。

sentences.en: So when Jarek was a kid in the 70s and 80s, Poland was a communist country.
sentences.zh: 当雅雷克在70和80年代还是个孩子时，波兰是一个共产主义国家。

sentences.en: It was part of the Soviet bloc.
sentences.zh: 它是苏联集团的一部分。

sentences.en: One month of martial law has not solved Poland's acute food crisis, and private Western agencies are rushing to help.
sentences.zh: 一个月的戒严令并没有解决波兰严重的粮食危机，私人西方机构正赶来援助。

sentences.en: And at the time, the Polish economy was struggling.
sentences.zh: 当时，波兰经济陷入困境。

sentences.en: Wages were stagnating.
sentences.zh: 工资停滞不前。

sentences.en: The media was censored.
sentences.zh: 媒体受到审查。

sentences.en: And a lot of people longed for more freedom.
sentences.zh: 许多人渴望更多的自由。

sentences.en: The police shot to people, and there was the victims and that.
sentences.zh: 警察向人们开枪，造成了伤亡。

sentences.en: And then this movement started.
sentences.zh: 然后这场运动开始了。

sentences.en: This movement against communism.
sentences.zh: 这场反共产主义的运动。

sentences.en: It was called Solidarity.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“团结工会”。

sentences.en: The new Solidarity movement was born last summer.
sentences.zh: 新的团结工会运动诞生于去年夏天。

sentences.en: It started with a group of shipyard workers in Gdansk, a city on the Baltic Sea, Jarek's hometown.
sentences.zh: 它始于波罗的海城市、雅雷克的家乡格但斯克的一群造船厂工人。

sentences.en: When striking workers forced the communist government to grant many concessions.
sentences.zh: 当时罢工工人迫使共产主义政府做出了许多让步。

sentences.en: Jarek was a teenager when all this was going on.
sentences.zh: 这一切发生时，雅雷克还是个少年。

sentences.en: And he and his younger brother, Jacek, saw all of this happening right in front of them as this movement was growing.
sentences.zh: 他和弟弟雅切克亲眼目睹了这一切，看着这场运动不断壮大。

sentences.en: And they took part in it.
sentences.zh: 他们也参与其中。

sentences.en: I take my bicycle and put the cigarettes and sandwich to the people who participated in this trade.
sentences.zh: 我骑着自行车，给参加这场贸易的人送香烟和三明治。

sentences.en: They also wrote for this illegal student newspaper, an anti-communist student newspaper.
sentences.zh: 他们还为一份非法的学生报纸、一份反共的学生报纸撰稿。

sentences.en: And later they wrote for another newspaper linked to the Solidarity movement itself.
sentences.zh: 后来他们又为另一份与团结工会运动本身有关的报纸撰稿。

sentences.en: They did everything they could to support the movement.
sentences.zh: 他们竭尽所能支持这场运动。

sentences.en: And all across Poland, the support for this movement, for Solidarity, was growing.
sentences.zh: 在整个波兰，对这场运动、对团结工会的支持日益高涨。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: Leading the news this Wednesday, Poland's Solidarity Union was legalized, a move that will end the communist monopoly of power.
sentences.zh: 本周三新闻头条，波兰团结工会获得合法化，此举将终结共产党的权力垄断。

sentences.en: And in the end, the movement prevailed.
sentences.zh: 最终，运动取得了胜利。

sentences.en: Communism fell.
sentences.zh: 共产主义垮台了。

sentences.en: And Poland became a democracy.
sentences.zh: 波兰成为了一个民主国家。

sentences.en: Poland was the most free country in the Soviet blocs.
sentences.zh: 波兰是苏联集团中最自由的国家。

sentences.en: And at that important moment in Poland, the Gazeta Wyborszka was born.
sentences.zh: 就在波兰那个重要的时刻，《选举报》诞生了。

sentences.en: This was Poland's first free, non-communist newspaper since World War II.
sentences.zh: 这是二战以来波兰第一份自由的、非共产主义的报纸。

sentences.en: Have you been at the newspaper from the start, when it first started 30 years ago?
sentences.zh: 你从报纸创办之初就在这里工作了吗，30年前刚开始的时候？

sentences.en: Have you been here?
sentences.zh: 你一直在这里吗？

sentences.en: Jarek started working there just a few years after the newspaper started.
sentences.zh: 雅雷克在报纸创办几年后就开始在那里工作了。

sentences.en: As a reporter or as an editor?
sentences.zh: 是作为记者还是编辑？

sentences.en: As a reporter.
sentences.zh: 作为记者。

sentences.en: And Jarek said the Gazeta Wyborszka had become the voice of a liberal democratic Poland.
sentences.zh: 雅雷克说，《选举报》已经成为自由民主波兰的代言人。

sentences.en: And as the paper was growing, so was Poland's economy.
sentences.zh: 随着报纸的发展，波兰的经济也在增长。

sentences.en: And then in 2004, Poland joined the European Union.
sentences.zh: 2004年，波兰加入了欧盟。

sentences.en: And this helped develop the country even more.
sentences.zh: 这进一步促进了国家的发展。

sentences.en: You have the European flag in your house?
sentences.zh: 你家里有欧盟旗帜吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, in my house.
sentences.zh: 有的，在我家里。

sentences.en: And once Poland joined the EU, the economy improved.
sentences.zh: 波兰加入欧盟后，经济得到了改善。

sentences.en: Life improved for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 许多人的生活得到了改善。

sentences.en: The country opened up.
sentences.zh: 国家开放了。

sentences.en: Wages went up.
sentences.zh: 工资上涨了。

sentences.en: People could travel.
sentences.zh: 人们可以去旅行了。

sentences.en: But there was another narrative that started to play out across the country, especially in rural areas.
sentences.zh: 但全国各地，特别是在农村地区，开始出现另一种叙事。

sentences.en: In the countryside and in smaller towns, the transition from communism to capitalism had proved particularly painful.
sentences.zh: 在农村和小城镇，从共产主义向资本主义的过渡被证明尤其痛苦。

sentences.en: These state-run businesses and farms had closed down with the fall of communism.
sentences.zh: 随着共产主义的垮台，这些国有企业和农场关闭了。

sentences.en: And there was often mass unemployment for a period of time.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间出现了大规模失业。

sentences.en: And a lot of people there felt left behind.
sentences.zh: 那里许多人感到被遗忘了。

sentences.en: These people have been watching their country change.
sentences.zh: 这些人一直在看着他们的国家发生变化。

sentences.en: They've been watching as church attendance rates have been falling, as gender equality and LGBT rights and other sort of liberal ideas are taking hold.
sentences.zh: 他们看着教堂出席率下降，看着性别平等、LGBT权利和其他一些自由主义思想占据主导地位。

sentences.en: They worry about their familiar old way of life changing.
sentences.zh: 他们担心自己熟悉的生活方式会改变。

sentences.en: They worry about their values being diluted.
sentences.zh: 他们担心自己的价值观被稀释。

sentences.en: They worry about losing what it is to be Polish.
sentences.zh: 他们担心失去作为波兰人的本质。

sentences.en: And they blame the EU.
sentences.zh: 他们把责任归咎于欧盟。

sentences.en: And out of this frustration, a new political party was born.
sentences.zh: 在这种挫败感中，一个新的政党诞生了。

sentences.en: Law and Justice, or Peace, PIS in Polish.
sentences.zh: 法律与公正党，简称PIS。

sentences.en: The party promises to represent these people.
sentences.zh: 该党承诺代表这些人。

sentences.en: It's a message that resonates.
sentences.zh: 这是一个引起共鸣的信息。

sentences.en: And Jarek's own brother is one of these people.
sentences.zh: 雅雷克的亲兄弟就是这些人中的一员。

sentences.en: So Jarek goes into journalism.
sentences.zh: 雅雷克投身于新闻业。

sentences.en: But his brother pursues a career in politics.
sentences.zh: 但他兄弟追求的是政治生涯。

sentences.en: And the two drift apart politically.
sentences.zh: 两人在政治上渐行渐远。

sentences.en: And in 2015, just as this migrant crisis unfolds in the rest of Europe, this conservative nationalist party wins the majority.
sentences.zh: 2015年，就在欧洲其他地区移民危机爆发之际，这个保守的民族主义政党赢得了多数席位。

sentences.en: And it becomes the first single party to control the government in Poland since the end of communism.
sentences.zh: 它成为自共产主义结束以来波兰第一个控制政府的单一政党。

sentences.en: And up until this point, the Gazeta Wyborszka is basically Poland's main daily newspaper.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，《选举报》基本上是波兰的主要日报。

sentences.en: But Jarek says that once this new party is in power, things start to change almost immediately.
sentences.zh: 但雅雷克说，一旦这个新政党上台，情况几乎立即开始发生变化。

sentences.en: And the first event that he sort of recalled this kind of ominous warning sign was that one day, when he was at work in the newsroom, they were having this office party.
sentences.zh: 他回忆起第一个不祥的警告信号是有一天，当他在新闻编辑室工作时，他们正在举行办公室聚会。

sentences.en: It was a singer and a concert.
sentences.zh: 有歌手和音乐会。

sentences.en: And while this was happening, a priest showed up outside the office, a priest who supported the new government.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，一位支持新政府的牧师出现在办公室外。

sentences.en: And this priest had come to stage an exorcism, an exorcism of the newspaper.
sentences.zh: 这位牧师来这里是为了进行驱魔，对报社进行驱魔。

sentences.en: He was there to exorcise the devilish spirits of liberalism from the building.
sentences.zh: 他在那里是为了驱逐大楼里自由主义的魔鬼精神。

sentences.en: And what starts as a kind of bizarre, absurd, almost funny scene becomes increasingly threatening because the crowd is growing.
sentences.zh: 起初这种怪异、荒谬、几乎滑稽的场景变得越来越具有威胁性，因为人群在增加。

sentences.en: It's chanting.
sentences.zh: 他们在高呼口号。

sentences.en: And it's becoming more aggressive.
sentences.zh: 而且变得越来越激进。

sentences.en: It's chanting about the paper promoting Islamic terrorism, promoting LGBT rights,
sentences.zh: 他们高呼报纸宣扬伊斯兰恐怖主义、宣扬LGBT权利、

sentences.en: promoting a transformation of Polish society.
sentences.zh: 宣扬波兰社会的转型。

sentences.en: The crowd becomes so threatening.
sentences.zh: 人群变得极具威胁性。

sentences.en: Jarek tells us the police had to secure the building.
sentences.zh: 雅雷克告诉我们，警察不得不保护大楼的安全。

sentences.en: So very soon, after this very public exorcism, Jarek told us that the government started to go directly after the media.
sentences.zh: 所以在这场公开的驱魔仪式后不久，雅雷克告诉我们，政府开始直接针对媒体。

sentences.en: And the first thing they did is they took over the state broadcasters.
sentences.zh: 他们做的第一件事就是接管国家广播机构。

sentences.en: So radio and television stations that were owned by the state, but had previously had editorial independents, kind of like the BBC,
sentences.zh: 因此，那些由国家拥有但此前拥有编辑独立性（有点像英国广播公司）的广播和电视台，

sentences.en: were now basically controlled by this government.
sentences.zh: 现在基本上由这个政府控制了。

sentences.en: They came in, they fired journalists, they put in their own, and they brought in a new chairman.
sentences.zh: 他们进驻后，解雇了记者，安插了自己的人，并带来了一位新董事长。

sentences.en: Someone who supported the government.
sentences.zh: 一个支持政府的人。

sentences.en: Jarek's own brother.
sentences.zh: 雅雷克的亲兄弟。

sentences.en: So as soon as he took over, he started running news and segments that were basically in line with the values of the party.
sentences.zh: 所以他一上任，就开始播放基本上符合该党价值观的新闻和节目。

sentences.en: Anti-Islam, anti-migration, anti-LGBT, anti-press, and anti-EU.
sentences.zh: 反伊斯兰、反移民、反LGBT、反媒体和反欧盟。

sentences.en: Once the state media were under control,
sentences.zh: 一旦国家媒体受到控制，

sentences.en: the government went directly after the independent press.
sentences.zh: 政府直接对独立媒体下手了。

sentences.en: And for Gazeta Vyborszka, Jarek's newspaper, he says this meant that basically all the subscriptions and all the advertising linked to any government-affiliated office
sentences.zh: 对于雅雷克的报纸《选举报》来说，他说这意味着基本上所有与政府附属机构相关的订阅和广告，

sentences.en: or enterprise were cut.
sentences.zh: 或者企业都被切断了。

sentences.en: When was that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么时候？

sentences.en: When was that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么时候？

sentences.en: It was 15, 15, December, 15, January, 16.
Gas stations run by the government were instructed to hide the Gazeta Vyborszka to make it more difficult to find if customers wanted to buy it.
sentences.zh: 政府经营的加油站接到指示，要将《选举报》藏起来，让想买的顾客更难找到。

sentences.en: Can I just ask you in terms of the impact, the financial impact, can you quantify that?
sentences.zh: 我能问一下关于影响，财务方面的影响，你能量化一下吗？

sentences.en: Can you sort of give an idea of, I don't know, you lost in one day, you lost, I don't know, half of your subscriptions or like a third or 10% or whatever it was?
sentences.zh: 你能大概给个概念吗，我不知道，你一天之内损失了，我不知道，是一半的订阅量，还是三分之一，或者10%，不管是多少？

sentences.en: He said he doesn't know exact numbers, but he said it was huge.
sentences.zh: 他说他不知道确切的数字，但他说损失非常巨大。

sentences.en: The government is using its power to try to strangle the newspaper.
sentences.zh: 政府正在利用权力试图扼杀这家报纸。

sentences.en: And then they're starting to sue journalists.
sentences.zh: 然后他们开始起诉记者。

sentences.en: It starts suing the paper.
sentences.zh: 开始起诉报社。

sentences.en: It starts suing individual journalists.
sentences.zh: 开始起诉个别记者。

sentences.en: Jarek tells us that there have been at least 30 cases against the paper.
sentences.zh: 雅雷克告诉我们，针对该报的诉讼至少有30起。

sentences.en: And that means that journalists are operating in this environment of intimidation on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 这意味着记者们每天都在这种恐吓的环境下工作。

sentences.en: So at some point, the newspaper starts referring to itself as the opposition.
sentences.zh: 所以到了一定程度，报纸开始称自己为反对派。

sentences.en: So we're back to a historical moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我们回到了一个历史时刻。

sentences.en: A crucial moment, no.
sentences.zh: 一个关键时刻，不是吗。

sentences.en: One second.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: The opposition to the government, just like they were the opposition to communism 30 years ago.
sentences.zh: 政府的反对派，就像他们30年前是共产主义的反对派一样。

sentences.en: That's not usually the role for a free and independent newspaper in a democracy.
sentences.zh: 这通常不是民主国家中自由独立报纸的角色。

sentences.en: The paper would say they have no choice in this moment but to fight back and that they'll drop opposition from their name as soon as law and justice is out of power.
sentences.zh: 报社方面会说，他们此刻别无选择，只能反击，而且一旦法律与公正党下台，他们就会把“反对派”这个词从名字中去掉。

sentences.en: But I'm struck that just by calling itself the opposition, they are actually contributing to this divide in Poland.
sentences.zh: 但我感到震惊的是，仅仅因为自称为反对派，他们实际上正在加剧波兰的这种分裂。

sentences.en: And that's basically where things stand today.
sentences.zh: 这就是目前的情况。

sentences.en: The divisions in Poland run really, really deep.
sentences.zh: 波兰的分裂真的非常、非常深。

sentences.en: Me and my brother, we served as an example of this clivage, this plate.
sentences.zh: 我和我兄弟，我们就是这种裂痕、这种板块的缩影。

sentences.en: We were hoping to interview your brother, but he hasn't really responded.
sentences.zh: 我们本希望能采访你兄弟，但他并没有真正回应。

sentences.en: It's obvious for me, he refused to have the interview with any international, broad newspaper and media.
sentences.zh: 对我来说很明显，他拒绝接受任何国际性的大型报纸和媒体的采访。

sentences.en: He was a supporter of Solidarity then.
sentences.zh: 他当时是团结工会的支持者。

sentences.en: When did it turn?
sentences.zh: 他是什么时候转变的？

sentences.en: When did he turn?
sentences.zh: 他是什么时候转变的？

sentences.en: Do you have a night?
sentences.zh: 你有时间吗？

sentences.en: I mean, this story of Jarek and his brother, it's kind of an incredible story.
sentences.zh: 我是说，雅雷克和他兄弟的故事，这真是一个不可思议的故事。

sentences.en: They don't talk to each other.
sentences.zh: 他们互不说话。

sentences.en: They haven't talked in years.
sentences.zh: 他们已经多年没说过话了。

sentences.en: Jarek can barely talk about his brother.
sentences.zh: 雅雷克几乎无法谈论他的兄弟。

sentences.en: It makes him too upset.
sentences.zh: 这让他太难过了。

sentences.en: And it seems crazy, right?
sentences.zh: 这看起来很疯狂，对吧？

sentences.en: This one brother running a liberal newspaper and this other brother running the state-controlled broadcaster.
sentences.zh: 一个兄弟经营着一家自由派报纸，另一个兄弟经营着国家控制的广播公司。

sentences.en: But it's not an uncommon story in Poland.
sentences.zh: 但这在波兰并不罕见。

sentences.en: These divisions run right across families.
sentences.zh: 这些分裂贯穿了整个家庭。

sentences.en: They run through friendships.
sentences.zh: 它们贯穿了友谊。

sentences.en: And people literally stop talking for life.
sentences.zh: 人们甚至会一辈子不再说话。

sentences.en: Jarek thinks this is all incredibly dangerous.
sentences.zh: 雅雷克认为这一切极其危险。

sentences.en: Because he thinks that the kind of propaganda that is coming out of the state-controlled broadcasters is fueling hatred.
sentences.zh: 因为他认为国家控制的广播公司散布的那种宣传正在煽动仇恨。

sentences.en: The atmosphere, atmosphere was created.
sentences.zh: 这种氛围，这种氛围被制造了出来。

sentences.en: And if you are the responsible to this propaganda, you have to take on consideration the possible consequences.
sentences.zh: 如果你要为这种宣传负责，你就必须考虑可能产生的后果。

sentences.en: And Jarek tells us about something that happened in his hometown of Gdansk earlier this year.
sentences.zh: 雅雷克告诉我们今年早些时候在他家乡格但斯克发生的一件事。

sentences.en: Something that he said could be seen as a kind of direct consequence of all this hatred.
sentences.zh: 他说这件事可以被视为所有这些仇恨的一种直接后果。

sentences.en: And so we went to Gdansk to hear that story.
sentences.zh: 所以我们去了格但斯克去听那个故事。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So we get to Gdansk and we head over to this Catholic church at the center of town to meet Magdalena Adamovic.
sentences.zh: 我们到达格但斯克，前往市中心的一座天主教堂去见玛格达莱娜·阿达莫维奇。
zh_words: 玛格达莱娜·阿达莫维奇

sentences.en: Do you come to this church for mass?
sentences.zh: 你来这座教堂做弥撒吗？

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: This is the basilic.
sentences.zh: 这是大教堂。

sentences.en: This is the biggest church in the world built by bricks.
sentences.zh: 这是世界上用砖块建造的最大的教堂。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Or out of bricks.
sentences.zh: 或者说是用砖块砌成的。

sentences.en: And here my husband is buried.
sentences.zh: 我丈夫就葬在这里。

sentences.en: So this is the story.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是故事。

sentences.en: Here, we're just outside.
sentences.zh: 这里，我们就在外面。

sentences.en: We're parking outside, okay?
sentences.zh: 我们把车停在外面，好吗？

sentences.en: Outside the gate.
sentences.zh: 在大门外。

sentences.en: So she invites us to her apartment and shows us into the living room where we sit down with some tea and some cookies.
sentences.zh: 她邀请我们去她的公寓，带我们走进客厅，我们坐下来喝茶吃饼干。

sentences.en: I will serve a little one.
sentences.zh: 我来端一点。

sentences.en: We call them Magdalene.
sentences.zh: 我们叫它们玛格达莱娜。

sentences.en: Magdalene's.
sentences.zh: 玛格达莱娜饼干。

sentences.en: And she starts telling us about her late husband, Pavel Adamovic, who was mayor of Gdansk for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 她开始向我们讲述她已故的丈夫帕维尔·阿达莫维奇，他曾担任格但斯克市长20年。

sentences.en: My husband was before a conservative person.
sentences.zh: 我丈夫以前是个保守的人。

sentences.en: He was considered to be a conservative?
sentences.zh: 他被认为是保守派？

sentences.en: Yeah, he was like a conservative person.
sentences.zh: 是的，他就像个保守的人。

sentences.en: He stood as a conservative and he represented conservative values to the point of banning gay pride in Gdansk in the early years.
sentences.zh: 他以保守派身份参选，并代表保守派价值观，甚至在早年禁止了格但斯克的同性恋骄傲游行。

sentences.en: But he was someone, she said, who always challenged his own views and was happy to listen to other people's opinions.
sentences.zh: 但她说，他是一个总是挑战自己观点，并乐于倾听他人意见的人。

sentences.en: He observed the people.
sentences.zh: 他观察人们。

sentences.en: He observed not only, you know, the infrastructure, but what the people are doing, how they react, what is the culture, what is the tradition.
sentences.zh: 他观察的不仅仅是基础设施，还有人们在做什么，他们如何反应，什么是文化，什么是传统。

sentences.en: So she said, for example, he would speak to people in Gdansk and scribble down notes whenever somebody said something that surprised him or challenged him.
sentences.zh: 所以她说，例如，他会和格但斯克的人交谈，每当有人说出让他惊讶或挑战他的话时，他就会记下笔记。

sentences.en: Yes, he always have some, you know, small papers in his pocket here and always, you know, put some notes.
sentences.zh: 是的，他口袋里总是装着一些小纸片，总是记下一些笔记。

sentences.en: Then he would come home at night and would take all these little scraps of paper out of his pockets and he would review them with a glass of wine and just make sure that he remembered what people had told him.
sentences.zh: 然后他晚上回家，会把这些小纸片从口袋里掏出来，一边喝着酒一边回顾，确保自己记住了人们告诉他的话。

sentences.en: Then after years, he changed and it took him some years.
sentences.zh: 后来过了几年，他变了，这花了他几年时间。

sentences.en: But when the nationalist government came into power in 2015 and started coming down hard on the LGBT community, he shifted on that issue.
sentences.zh: 但当民族主义政府在2015年上台并开始严厉打击LGBT群体时，他在这个问题上转变了立场。

sentences.en: He said, no, we cannot allow to treat these people as a sick people because they were considered by our government as a sick,
sentences.zh: 他说，不，我们不能允许把这些人当作病人来对待，因为他们被我们的政府视为病人，

sentences.en: as a people who are dangerous because of diseases and so on.
sentences.zh: 被视为因为疾病等原因而危险的人。

sentences.en: And in 2017, he not only allowed Gay Pride, but he marched.
sentences.zh: 2017年，他不仅允许了同性恋骄傲游行，还亲自参加了。

sentences.en: And when he took part in this LGBT parade, Gay Pride, was there a backlash?
sentences.zh: 当他参加这个LGBT游行，即同性恋骄傲游行时，有反弹吗？

sentences.en: Yes, there was some hate on him.
sentences.zh: 是的，有人对他怀有仇恨。

sentences.en: For example, national TV did over 100 programs, showing my husband as a thief, as a liar.
sentences.zh: 例如，国家电视台做了100多个节目，把我的丈夫描绘成一个小偷、一个骗子。

sentences.en: He became a target on state television.
sentences.zh: 他成了国家电视台的目标。

sentences.en: But even as his views shifted, Pavel was still re-elected.
sentences.zh: 但即使他的观点发生了转变，帕维尔仍然再次当选。

sentences.en: And in 2018, he began a sixth term as mayor of Gdansk.
sentences.zh: 2018年，他开始了格但斯克市长的第六个任期。

sentences.en: So I went to California at the end of November.
sentences.zh: 所以我11月底去了加利福尼亚。

sentences.en: Around this time, Magdalena was in California with their two daughters.
sentences.zh: 大约在这个时候，玛格达莱娜和他们的两个女儿在加利福尼亚。

sentences.en: And Pavel joined them for a family vacation.
sentences.zh: 帕维尔也加入了他们，进行了一次家庭度假。

sentences.en: And that has never, ever happened before, that we were all together so long without his job, without any, let's say, friends and duties.
sentences.zh: 那是以前从未发生过的事情，我们在一起待了那么久，没有他的工作，没有朋友和职责。

sentences.en: So it was a very special time for us, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以那对我们来说是一段非常特别的时光。

sentences.en: After a couple of weeks, Pavel had to head back home because he had business to attend to as mayor.
sentences.zh: 几周后，帕维尔不得不赶回家，因为他有作为市长的公务要处理。

sentences.en: And Magdalena stayed behind with their daughters.
sentences.zh: 玛格达莱娜和女儿们留在了那里。

sentences.en: And then he called her early in the morning, soon after he got back.
sentences.zh: 然后他在清晨给她打了电话，就在他回去后不久。

sentences.en: I had some nightmares.
sentences.zh: 我做了一些噩梦。

sentences.en: And he said he'd had nightmares that night.
sentences.zh: 他说他那天晚上做了噩梦。

sentences.en: And he couldn't really sleep.
sentences.zh: 他真的睡不着。

sentences.en: And he didn't know.
sentences.zh: 他不知道为什么。

sentences.en: Maybe it was the jet lag.
sentences.zh: 也许是时差。

sentences.en: And I said to him, he told me goodbye.
sentences.zh: 我对他说，他跟我说了再见。

sentences.en: It was a short conversation.
sentences.zh: 那是一次简短的谈话。

sentences.en: And they say goodbye.
sentences.zh: 他们说了再见。

sentences.en: And then Magdalena goes to church later in the day and takes her daughters.
sentences.zh: 然后玛格达莱娜当天晚些时候去教堂，带着她的女儿们。

sentences.en: She turns off her phone during the service.
sentences.zh: 她在礼拜期间关掉了手机。

sentences.en: And when she comes back out, I turn it on and I saw my niece was calling three times.
sentences.zh: 当她出来时，我打开手机，看到我侄女打了三个电话。

sentences.en: She realizes she has a ton of missed calls.
sentences.zh: 她意识到自己有很多未接来电。

sentences.en: So she calls her niece back.
sentences.zh: 于是她回拨给侄女。

sentences.en: And her niece tells her that her husband has been stabbed.
sentences.zh: 侄女告诉她，她丈夫被刺伤了。

sentences.en: I thought, it's not true.
sentences.zh: 我想，这不是真的。

sentences.en: And I was starting to call all his deputy mayors, you know, one and the other one.
sentences.zh: 我开始给所有的副市长打电话，一个接一个。

sentences.en: And nobody answered, nobody answered.
sentences.zh: 没人接，没人接。

sentences.en: I said, OK, this is winter.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，现在是冬天。

sentences.en: He has, you know, a thick jacket.
sentences.zh: 他穿着厚夹克。

sentences.en: And probably he's only a little wounded, you know, and nothing happened.
sentences.zh: 可能他只是受了点轻伤，什么事都没有。

sentences.en: It is winter.
sentences.zh: 现在是冬天。

sentences.en: He would have worn a thick winter jacket.
sentences.zh: 他应该穿了厚厚的冬装夹克。

sentences.en: He's probably in a very good hospital.
sentences.zh: 他可能在一家很好的医院。

sentences.en: It's probably all going to be fine.
sentences.zh: 可能一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: But then more calls start coming in.
sentences.zh: 但随后更多的电话打了进来。

sentences.en: And she's beginning to realize that this actually happened, that her husband was stabbed.
sentences.zh: 她开始意识到这真的发生了，她的丈夫被刺伤了。

sentences.en: In Gdansk, on stage.
sentences.zh: 在格但斯克，在舞台上。

sentences.en: He was stabbed in the heart.
sentences.zh: 他心脏被刺中了。

sentences.en: I really didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: I called my agent to find tickets.
sentences.zh: 我打电话给我的代理人找机票。

sentences.en: Eventually, she finds an indirect flight via London, gets on it.
sentences.zh: 最终，她找到了一班经由伦敦的中转航班，登上了飞机。

sentences.en: So all the way, you know, we were, like, praying that he would be alive.
sentences.zh: 所以一路上，我们都在祈祷他能活着。

sentences.en: And then she lands in Gdansk.
sentences.zh: 然后她降落在格但斯克。

sentences.en: She's picked up at the airport and she's told that her husband is already dead.
sentences.zh: 她在机场被接走，并被告知她的丈夫已经去世了。

sentences.en: So she goes to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 于是她去了医院。

sentences.en: And she sits with his body.
sentences.zh: 她坐在他的遗体旁。

sentences.en: So I have to unzip him.
sentences.zh: 我不得不拉开他的拉链。

sentences.en: And I was talking to him, telling goodbye.
sentences.zh: 我当时在和他说话，向他告别。

sentences.en: Touching him, kissing him.
sentences.zh: 触摸他，亲吻他。

sentences.en: What did you tell him?
sentences.zh: 你对他说了什么？

sentences.en: Why, why he, why he left us?
sentences.zh: 为什么，为什么他，为什么他离开了我们？

sentences.en: Why he left us?
sentences.zh: 为什么他离开了我们？

sentences.en: That we need him.
sentences.zh: 我们需要他。

sentences.en: The man who stabbed Pavel, Adamovich, was a mentally unstable individual.
sentences.zh: 刺杀帕维尔的凶手阿达莫维奇是一个精神不稳定的人。

sentences.en: He'd been in an institution.
sentences.zh: 他曾被关在精神病院里。

sentences.en: But in that institution, he'd been exposed to a lot of state television.
sentences.zh: 但在那家机构里，他接触了大量国家电视台的节目。

sentences.en: And this is one thing that leads Magdalena to think pretty much immediately.
sentences.zh: 这就是玛格达莱娜几乎立刻就产生某种想法的原因。

sentences.en: That her husband was killed by an atmosphere of hate.
sentences.zh: 她认为她的丈夫是被一种仇恨氛围所杀害的。

sentences.en: She blames the media.
sentences.zh: 她指责媒体。

sentences.en: She blames what she called institutionalized hate speech on the public broadcaster.
sentences.zh: 她指责公共广播机构中所谓的体制化仇恨言论。

sentences.en: I think it is polarization.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是两极分化。

sentences.en: Without that, I believe my husband would still be alive.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这些，我相信我的丈夫现在还活着。

sentences.en: Polarization killed him.
sentences.zh: 两极分化杀了他。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I thought, I have to do something.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，我必须做点什么。

sentences.en: His death cannot be waste, you know.
sentences.zh: 他的死不能毫无意义，你知道的。

sentences.en: She decides to run for office.
sentences.zh: 她决定参加竞选。

sentences.en: She decides to run for a seat in the European Parliament.
sentences.zh: 她决定竞选欧洲议会的一个席位。

sentences.en: What is it that you, if you get elected, what is it that you want to change?
sentences.zh: 如果你当选了，你想要改变什么？

sentences.en: So what I'm afraid, it's that nationalists and the people who are really against the European Union and would like to blow up the European Union from inside.
sentences.zh: 我担心的是，那些民族主义者，以及那些真正反对欧盟、想要从内部摧毁欧盟的人。

sentences.en: It can happen everywhere, you know.
sentences.zh: 这在任何地方都可能发生，你知道的。

sentences.en: She told us of her grandmother and her great-grandmother, who had both survived Auschwitz.
sentences.zh: 她向我们讲述了她的祖母和曾祖母，她们都曾从奥斯威辛集中营幸存下来。

sentences.en: If you divide people, if you differ the people between them, if you think that someone is better than the other, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果你分裂民众，如果你在他们之间制造差异，如果你认为某些人比其他人更优越，你知道的，

sentences.en: then you can have the same story as it was before, you know.
sentences.zh: 那么历史就可能会重演，你知道的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: So we say goodbye to Magdalena, and we reached out to the Law and Justice Party to basically find someone to ask this question to.
sentences.zh: 我们告别了玛格达莱娜，并联系了法律与公正党，想找个人来回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Is this government and the state-controlled media, are they creating an atmosphere so full of hatred and so full of division
sentences.zh: 这个政府和受国家控制的媒体，是否正在营造一种充满仇恨和分裂的氛围，

sentences.en: that it may have inspired the murder of Magdalena's husband?
sentences.zh: 以至于可能诱发了对玛格达莱娜丈夫的谋杀？

sentences.en: And we meet Danuta, Danuta Bialuka-Konstaneka, a local official from the Law and Justice Party.
sentences.zh: 我们见到了达努塔，达努塔·比亚卢卡-康斯坦卡，她是法律与公正党的一名地方官员。

sentences.en: I prefer to speak through the interpreter.
sentences.zh: 我更愿意通过翻译来交流。

sentences.en: We meet her at our hotel in Gdansk.
sentences.zh: 我们在格但斯克的酒店见到了她。

sentences.en: She's very conservatively dressed, elegant, and she has this kind of nervous laugh.
sentences.zh: 她穿着非常保守、优雅，带着一种神经质的笑声。

sentences.en: And I asked Danuta, do you think that your party's discourse contributes to an environment in which societies become very polarized
sentences.zh: 我问达努塔，你是否认为你们党的言论导致了社会变得极度两极分化，

sentences.en: and a deranged individual might have the idea to stab a mayor on stage?
sentences.zh: 以至于一个精神错乱的人可能会产生在舞台上刺杀市长的想法？

sentences.en: Now, it was interesting because Danuta did not dispute
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为达努塔并没有否认

sentences.en: that there was a lot of division in Poland.
sentences.zh: 波兰存在严重的分裂。

sentences.en: She did not dispute even that the state-controlled media was blatantly biased in favor of the government.
sentences.zh: 她甚至没有否认受国家控制的媒体在明显偏袒政府。

sentences.en: But she rejected the idea that the murder had in any way been inspired by that atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 但她拒绝接受谋杀以任何方式受到那种氛围影响的说法。

sentences.en: She claimed that this had simply been the act of a mentally unstable individual and that the division in society, which she also considered a problem,
sentences.zh: 她声称这仅仅是一个精神不稳定者的个人行为，而她也认为社会分裂是一个问题，

sentences.en: was the fault of all sides involved.
sentences.zh: 但这是各方共同造成的。

sentences.en: And the Law and Justice Party is changing Poland.
sentences.zh: 法律与公正党正在改变波兰。

sentences.en: What does the party stand for?
sentences.zh: 该党的主张是什么？

sentences.en: And she basically said,
sentences.zh: 她基本上是这样说的，

sentences.en: we're Polish and we want to stay Polish.
sentences.zh: 我们是波兰人，我们想保持波兰人的身份。

sentences.en: We want Poland to stay Polish.
sentences.zh: 我们希望波兰保持波兰特色。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: It's a different question.
sentences.zh: 这是另一个问题。

sentences.en: It's more of a philosophical question.
sentences.zh: 这更像是一个哲学问题。

sentences.en: I think there are certain things that all Polish people have in common, and that's language, culture, tradition, and history.
sentences.zh: 我认为所有波兰人都有一些共同点，那就是语言、文化、传统和历史。

sentences.en: And religion, I asked her, and she said, yes, religion too, Christianity.
sentences.zh: 我问她关于宗教的问题，她说，是的，宗教也是，基督教。

sentences.en: Can you be gay and atheist and Polish?
sentences.zh: 你可以既是同性恋、无神论者，又是波兰人吗？

sentences.en: Of course you can.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: She said her party doesn't tolerate discrimination.
sentences.zh: 她说她的党不容忍歧视。

sentences.en: But what she said she didn't like and what her party didn't want is what she called
sentences.zh: 但她说她不喜欢、她的党也不想要的是她所谓的

sentences.en: active promotion of those values.
sentences.zh: 对这些价值观的积极推广。

sentences.en: Is that what the mayor in Gdansk was doing?
sentences.zh: 格但斯克的市长是在做这件事吗？

sentences.en: By marching with gay pride?
sentences.zh: 通过参加同性恋骄傲游行？

sentences.en: Is it what allowing an openly gay person to teach in a school would be doing?
sentences.zh: 允许一个公开的同性恋者在学校教书是在做这件事吗？

sentences.en: Is it what letting someone be openly gay on the street would be doing?
sentences.zh: 让某人在街上公开表现出同性恋身份是在做这件事吗？

sentences.en: What does that phrase really mean?
sentences.zh: 那句话到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: Active promotion.
sentences.zh: 积极推广。

sentences.en: I think I'm done now.
sentences.zh: 我想我问完了。

sentences.en: So I thank her.
sentences.zh: 所以我感谢她。

sentences.en: We wrap up the interview, but she looks pretty exasperated.
sentences.zh: 我们结束了采访，但她看起来非常恼火。

sentences.en: So now we just take a photo.
sentences.zh: 现在我们拍张照吧。

sentences.en: It was very exhausting.
sentences.zh: 这太累人了。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: But it's so interesting.
sentences.zh: 但这非常有趣。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 真的很有趣。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, we need to understand everybody better.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，我们需要更好地理解每个人。

sentences.en: Would you mind?
sentences.zh: 你不介意吧？

sentences.en: I'm not quite happy because I have a feeling that you don't understand.
sentences.zh: 我不太高兴，因为我觉得你不理解。

sentences.en: Our point of view.
sentences.zh: 我们的观点。

sentences.en: Maybe we need to meet again.
sentences.zh: 也许我们需要再见一次。

sentences.en: Yeah, maybe.
sentences.zh: 是的，也许吧。

sentences.en: Talk some more.
sentences.zh: 再多聊聊。

sentences.en: What do you think we don't understand?
sentences.zh: 你觉得我们哪里不理解？

sentences.en: I think you're still thinking that our democracy is a threat and we are fighting for democracy.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你仍然认为我们的民主是一种威胁，而我们是在为民主而战。

sentences.en: I don't think that Poland is the same.
sentences.zh: 我不认为波兰的情况是一样的。

sentences.en: Do you think Hungary is a democracy?
sentences.zh: 你认为匈牙利是民主国家吗？

sentences.en: I ask her if she thinks Hungary is a democracy.
sentences.zh: 我问她是否认为匈牙利是一个民主国家。

sentences.en: Hungary has had a nationalist government for even longer than Poland.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利拥有民族主义政府的时间甚至比波兰还要长。

sentences.en: And there, the free press is pretty much entirely gone.
sentences.zh: 在那里，自由媒体几乎完全消失了。

sentences.en: And the country actually calls itself an illiberal democracy.
sentences.zh: 而且这个国家实际上自称为非自由民主国家。

sentences.en: A democracy that is no longer built on liberal values.
sentences.zh: 一个不再建立在自由主义价值观之上的民主国家。

sentences.en: Do you think Hungary is still a democracy?
sentences.zh: 你认为匈牙利现在还是民主国家吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And do you think Germany is a democracy?
sentences.zh: 你认为德国是民主国家吗？

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Come to me.
sentences.zh: 过来。

sentences.en: Do you think Germany is a democracy?
sentences.zh: 你认为德国是民主国家吗？

sentences.en: I think it is.
sentences.zh: 我认为是的。

sentences.en: But I can see some threat for democracy in Germany.
sentences.zh: 但我能看到德国的民主面临一些威胁。

sentences.en: And I'm beginning to realize she wants to take the liberalism out of democracy.
sentences.zh: 我开始意识到她想把自由主义从民主中剔除。

sentences.en: She thinks liberal democracy ultimately limits freedom.
sentences.zh: 她认为自由民主最终限制了自由。

sentences.en: She says having a system which guarantees freedom for the individual, that's just fine.
sentences.zh: 她说，拥有一个保障个人自由的制度，那很好。

sentences.en: But it's when that system is imposing specific behaviors on people that it's not right anymore.
sentences.zh: 但当这个制度强加给人们特定的行为时，它就不再正确了。

sentences.en: She says democracy should give people what they want and that that's what Poland is doing.
sentences.zh: 她说民主应该给人们他们想要的，而这正是波兰正在做的。

sentences.en: Her party was elected by a majority.
sentences.zh: 她的党是由多数人选出的。

sentences.en: And it's keeping its promises to that majority.
sentences.zh: 并且它正在履行对多数人的承诺。

sentences.en: Whereas a liberal democracy has these freedoms that aren't negotiable.
sentences.zh: 而自由民主拥有这些不可谈判的自由。

sentences.en: It imposes minority rights on the majority.
sentences.zh: 它将少数人的权利强加给多数人。

sentences.en: So we have this sort of moment at the end of this interview where these two opposing visions of democracy suddenly clash and just kind of sit side by side.
sentences.zh: 所以在采访结束时，我们出现了这样一种时刻：这两种对立的民主观突然发生碰撞，并排存在。

sentences.en: And honestly, I think this is the closest we've come to understanding what the battle for Europe's future is over.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为这是我们最接近理解欧洲未来之争焦点的一次。

sentences.en: However, it's not about democracy versus something else.
sentences.zh: 然而，这并非关于民主与其他事物的对立。

sentences.en: It's about these two opposing views of democracy.
sentences.zh: 这是关于这两种对立的民主观。

sentences.en: We've been coming at this like there's no such thing as democracy without liberalism.
sentences.zh: 我们一直认为没有自由主义就没有民主。

sentences.en: And she's saying, you've got it exactly wrong.
sentences.zh: 而她说，你们完全错了。

sentences.en: Liberalism is actually undemocratic.
sentences.zh: 自由主义实际上是不民主的。

sentences.en: It only allows for one perspective.
sentences.zh: 它只允许一种观点存在。

sentences.en: And in Poland, she's saying the majority of voters, not only do they not share that perspective, they voted against it.
sentences.zh: 而在波兰，她说大多数选民不仅不认同那种观点，他们还投票反对它。

sentences.en: That's democracy.
sentences.zh: 那才是民主。

sentences.en: I don't know the German society.
sentences.zh: 我不了解德国社会。

sentences.en: I have been to Germany a long time.
sentences.zh: 我去过德国很久了。

sentences.en: Germany, she says, not so much.
sentences.zh: 德国，她说，没那么了解。

sentences.en: And that's where we're going next.
sentences.zh: 而这就是我们接下来要去的地方。

sentences.en: Back to Germany.
sentences.zh: 回到德国。

sentences.en: To find out about the results
sentences.zh: 去了解这些欧盟选举的结果。

sentences.en: in these EU elections.
sentences.zh: 去看看欧洲是如何开始回答这个民主问题的。

sentences.en: To see how Europe is starting to answer this democracy question.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是卡特琳·本霍尔德。

sentences.en: I'm Katrin Benhold.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 在德国。

sentences.en: In Germany.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 他们需要完全遮光吗？

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或任何你喜欢的播客平台上收听《Wirecutter秀》。

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 再见。
